words.ex_cn: 这项研究的结果表明，睡眠有助于记忆。
words.en: The results of an investigation or research; something that is discovered.

words.tr: adj. 新兴的； v. 浮现；显露；“emerge”的现在分词；
words.ex: China has many emerging tech companies.
words.ex_cn: 中国有许多新兴的科技公司。
words.en: An emerging market, country, or economy is one that is beginning to grow and develop its industries and infrastructure.

words.tr: n. 雾月（法国共和历的第二个月，相当于公历10月22日至11月20日）
words.ex: He was born in brumaire, a month in the French revolutionary calendar.
words.ex_cn: 他出生在雾月，这是法国革命历法中的一个月份。
words.en: Brumaire is the second month of the French Republican Calendar, corresponding to October 22 to November 20 in the Gregorian calendar, known for its foggy weather.

words.tr: adj. 法兰克人的；法兰克语的
words.ex: The frankish king ruled over a small kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 法兰克国王统治着一个小王国。
words.en: Relating to the Franks or their language.

words.ex: The renewals for the subscriptions happen every year.
words.ex_cn: 订阅的续订每年都会进行。
words.en: Renewals refer to the act of making something valid or effective for an additional period, such as extending a subscription or contract.

words.tr:
n. 混乱；一团糟
v. 蹒跚地走；踉跄而行；“shamble”的第三人称单数
words.ex: The room was a complete shambles after the party.
words.ex_cn: 派对过后，房间一片狼藉。
words.en: A state of total disorder.

words.tr: n. 品牌营销；品牌化； v. “brand”的现在分词；
words.ex: The company spent money on branding to attract more customers.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司花钱做品牌营销以吸引更多的顾客。
words.en: The process of creating a unique name and image for a product in the consumers' mind, mainly through advertising campaigns with a consistent theme.

words.ex: The priests wore long black cassocks during the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 神父们在仪式上穿着长长的黑色长袍。
words.en: A cassock is a long, close-fitting garment worn by members of the clergy or other religious orders.

words.ex: He clumsily dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他笨拙地打翻了玻璃杯。
words.en: In a way that is awkward in movement or handling things.

words.ex: He carefully slid the sword into its scabbard.
words.ex_cn: 他小心地把剑插回鞘中。
words.en: A scabbard is a sheath for a sword, dagger, or other similar blade.

words.ex: My grandfather loves his grandson very much.
words.ex_cn: 我的祖父非常爱他的孙子。
words.en: A grandson is the son of your son or daughter.

words.ex: They held a big banquet after the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他们在婚礼后举办了一场盛大的宴会。
words.en: A banquet is a large formal meal for many people, often followed by speeches.

words.tr: n. 克里斯托弗·哥伦布（Christopher Columbus，意大利航海家）；哥伦布（美国俄亥俄州首府）；
words.ex: Columbus sailed across the Atlantic Ocean in 1492.
words.ex_cn: 哥伦布在1492年横渡大西洋。
words.en: Columbus was an Italian explorer who completed four voyages across the Atlantic Ocean, opening the way for the widespread European exploration and colonization of the Americas.

words.tr: adj. 讨厌的； v. “annoy”的现在分词；
words.ex: The loud noise is annoying.
words.ex_cn: 这噪音很讨厌。
words.en: Something that is annoying makes you feel fairly angry and impatient.

words.ex: The mephitic smell made everyone cover their noses.
words.ex_cn: 那股恶臭让所有人都捂住了鼻子。
words.en: Mephitic refers to something that is foul-smelling or poisonous, often used to describe gases or odors that are harmful or unpleasant.

words.ex: He said farewell to his friends before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前向朋友们道别。
words.en: Farewell is an expression of good wishes at parting, often used to say goodbye.

words.tr: n. 强烈的抗议或呼喊
words.ex: The people made outcries against the new law.
words.ex_cn: 人们对这项新法律发出抗议。
words.en: Loud expressions of protest or disapproval.

words.tr: adv. 精神上；思想上；智力上；
words.ex: He is mentally strong despite his challenges.
words.ex_cn: 尽管面临挑战，他在精神上很坚强。
words.en: In a manner relating to the mind or mental processes.

words.tr: adj. 边远的；偏远的；远离市镇的
words.ex: The outlying village has no bus service.
words.ex_cn: 这个偏远的村庄没有公交车服务。
words.en: Situated far from a center or main area.

words.tr: adj. <美俚>渐渐松驰的，渐渐不行了的，渐渐变懒的 v. 滑脱; 滑( slip的现在分词 );
words.ex: The rope is slipping out of my hand.
words.ex_cn: 绳子从我手中滑脱。
words.en: Moving or falling out of place; declining in quality or performance.

words.tr: n. 拼写；拼法； v. “spell”的现在分词；
words.ex: His spelling is very poor.
words.ex_cn: 他的拼写很差。
words.en: The forming of words from letters according to accepted usage; orthography.

words.tr: n. 方言；土语；方言，土语( dialect的名词复数 )；
words.ex: People in different villages speak different dialects.
words.ex_cn: 不同村庄的人说不同的方言。
words.en: Varieties of a language spoken in a particular region or by a particular group.

words.ex: Mr. Stapleton lives near the moor.
words.ex_cn: 斯塔普尔顿先生住在沼泽附近。
words.en: Stapleton is a surname of English origin, commonly found in the United Kingdom and other English-speaking countries.

words.ex: From the clues, he made a logical inference.
words.ex_cn: 从线索中，他做出了一个合理的推论。
words.en: An inference is a conclusion that you draw about something by using information that you already have about it.

words.tr: adj. 无限制的；无界限的；
words.ex: The sky looks limitless at night.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚的天空看起来无边无际。
words.en: If you describe something as limitless, you mean that there is or appears to be so much of it that it will never be exhausted.

words.ex: He is reversing the car slowly.
words.ex_cn: 他正在慢慢倒车。
words.en: To change something to its opposite direction, order, or position.

words.tr: n. 单独所有权；单独拥有的财产
words.ex: The land was held in severalty by the farmer.
words.ex_cn: 这块土地由农民单独所有。
words.en: The state of being separate or distinct; individual ownership of property.

words.ex: Unluckily, he missed the bus this morning.
words.ex_cn: 不幸的是，他今天早上错过了公交车。
words.en: In an unfortunate or unlucky manner.

words.tr: adj. 窘迫的；受辱的; v. 使受辱（mortify 的过去式）
words.ex: He was mortified when he forgot his lines on stage.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记舞台上的台词时，他感到羞愧至极。
words.en: If you say that someone is mortified, you mean that they feel extremely ashamed or humiliated.

words.ex: The invaders plundered the village and took all the valuables.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者洗劫了村庄，拿走了所有值钱的东西。
words.en: To plunder means to steal goods from a place or person, especially in a violent or destructive way, typically during a war or riot.

words.tr: v. 预测；预言；“predict”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The weather forecast predicted rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 天气预报预测明天有雨。
words.en: If you predict an event, you say that it will happen.

words.ex: The car runs on petroleum.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车使用石油运行。
words.en: A naturally occurring, yellow-to-black liquid found in geological formations beneath the Earth's surface, which is commonly refined into various types of fuels.

words.tr: v. 使减到最少；使缩到最小；
words.ex: He minimises waste by recycling.
words.ex_cn: 他通过回收利用把浪费降到最少。
words.en: To reduce something to the smallest possible amount or degree.

words.tr:
n. 西南；
adj. 位于西南的；
adv. 向西南；
words.ex: The storm came from the southwest.
words.ex_cn: 风暴来自西南方向。
words.en: The southwest is the direction which is halfway between south and west.

words.ex: Water and salt are common compounds.
words.ex_cn: 水和盐是常见的化合物。
words.en: A compound is a substance that consists of two or more elements chemically combined in fixed proportions.

words.tr:
n. 面试；访谈；
v. 面试；接见；
words.ex: He has an interview tomorrow for a new job.
words.ex_cn: 他明天有一场新工作的面试。
words.en: An interview is a formal meeting at which someone is asked questions in order to find out if they are suitable for a job or a course of study.

words.tr: n. 兰开斯特（美国成市）
words.ex: Lancaster is known for its rich history and cultural heritage.
words.ex_cn: 兰开斯特以其丰富的历史和文化遗产而闻名。
words.en: Lancaster is a city in the north of England, known for its historical significance and the Lancaster family, which played a crucial role in English history.

words.ex: The locksmith was able to pick the lock in just a few minutes.
words.ex_cn: 锁匠在几分钟内就能把锁打开。
words.en: A locksmith is a person whose job is making and repairing locks.

words.tr: adj. 残忍的；无情的；无慈悲心的；
words.ex: The merciless storm destroyed the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场残忍的风暴摧毁了村庄。
words.en: If you describe someone as merciless, you mean that they are very cruel or determined and do not show any concern for the effect their actions have on other people.

words.ex: The old shipwreck lies at the bottom of the sea.
words.ex_cn: 那艘旧船的残骸躺在海底。
words.en: A shipwreck is the destruction of a ship at sea by sinking or breaking up, for example in a storm or after hitting a rock.

words.ex: He showed obeisance to the king by bowing deeply.
words.ex_cn: 他通过深深鞠躬向国王表示敬意。
words.en: Obeisance is a gesture or movement of the body expressing respect or submission.

words.tr: adj. 专注的；专用的；献身的； v. 奉献；“dedicate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is dedicated to his studies.
words.ex_cn: 他专注于学习。
words.en: If you say that someone is dedicated to something, you approve of the fact that they have committed to it and are willing to give a lot of time and energy to it.

words.ex: The blood will coagulate if it is left outside the body.
words.ex_cn: 血液如果留在体外，就会凝结。
words.en: If a liquid coagulates, it becomes thick and almost solid.

words.ex: He got pneumonia after a bad cold.
words.ex_cn: 他得了重感冒后患了肺炎。
words.en: Pneumonia is a serious disease which affects your lungs and makes it difficult for you to breathe.

words.tr: adj. 丰富的，大量的 v. 大量存在，充满，富于( abound的现在分词 )
words.ex: The forest is abounding with wildlife.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林里充满了野生动物。
words.en: If something abounds in a particular place, it exists there in very large numbers or quantities.

words.ex: He is a physicist who studies stars.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位研究恒星的物理学家。
words.en: A physicist is a scientist who specializes in the field of physics, which is the study of matter, energy, and the fundamental forces of nature.

words.tr: v. 宣判，判决( sentence的过去式和过去分词 )
words.ex: The judge sentenced him to five years in prison.
words.ex_cn: 法官判他五年监禁。
words.en: To officially state that someone is to receive a particular punishment, especially after being found guilty of a crime.

words.ex: The priest christens the baby in the church.
words.ex_cn: 牧师在教堂里为婴儿施洗礼。
words.en: To christen means to perform the Christian religious ceremony of baptism on someone, or to give a name to something, especially a ship.

words.ex: The shipowner was responsible for the maintenance of the vessel.
words.ex_cn: 船主负责船只的维护。
words.en: A shipowner is a person or company that owns a ship or ships.

words.ex: The burglars ransacked the house looking for valuables.
words.ex_cn: v. 窃贼彻底搜查了房子寻找贵重物品。
words.en: To search a place thoroughly, often causing disorder or damage.

words.ex: He is known for his powerful preaching on Sunday mornings.
words.ex_cn: 他以周日早晨强有力的讲道而闻名。
words.en: The act of delivering a sermon or religious address to an assembled group of people, typically in church.

words.tr: n. 吝啬；小气；过度节俭
words.ex: His parsimony led to a reputation for stinginess.
words.ex_cn: 他的吝啬导致了他被认为是个小气鬼。
words.en: Parsimony is the quality of being very unwilling to spend money.

words.ex: The market demand for oil is inelastic.
words.ex_cn: 石油的市场需求是无弹性的。
words.en: If something is inelastic, it does not stretch or change shape easily when a force is applied to it, or it does not change much in price when the supply of it changes.

words.ex: The curvature of the road makes driving slow.
words.ex_cn: 道路的弯曲使驾驶变慢。
words.en: The curvature of something is the fact that it is curved or the degree to which it is curved.

words.tr: n. 崩溃；故障；细目分类；
words.ex: The stress led to a breakdown.
words.ex_cn: 压力导致了崩溃。
words.en: A breakdown is a failure of a system, machine, or relationship, or a sudden collapse in someone's mental health.

words.tr: n. 无辜者；天真无邪的人
words.ex: The law must protect the innocents from wrongful accusations.
words.ex_cn: 法律必须保护无辜者免受错误的指控。
words.en: Innocents refers to people who are not guilty of a crime or other wrongful act, or who are free from moral wrong; sinless.

words.tr: adj. 恐惧的；受惊吓的； v. “terrify”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The child was terrified of the dark.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子害怕黑暗。
words.en: If you are terrified, you are extremely frightened.

words.ex: The novel describes an adulterer who faces the consequences of his actions.
words.ex_cn: 这部小说描述了一个面临自己行为后果的通奸者。
words.en: An adulterer is a person who commits adultery; someone who has voluntary sexual intercourse with a married person who is not their spouse.

words.ex: He led a dissolute life after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后过着放荡的生活。
words.en: If you describe someone as dissolute, you mean they behave in a way that is considered immoral because they do things such as drink or have sex too much.

words.ex: He dropped his pretences and spoke honestly.
words.ex_cn: 他放下了伪装，坦诚地说话。
words.en: A pretence is an action or way of behaving that is intended to make people believe something that is not true.

words.ex: The plant needs phosphate to grow well.
words.ex_cn: 植物需要磷酸盐才能良好生长。
words.en: A phosphate is a salt or ester of phosphoric acid, containing the anion PO₄³⁻ or the group —PO₄.

words.tr: v. 扼死( strangle的过去式和过去分词 ); 使窒息; 抑制; 压制
words.ex: He was strangled by a rope.
words.ex_cn: 他被一根绳子勒死了。
words.en: If someone is strangled, they are killed by having something such as a cord or hands pressed tightly against their throat so that they cannot breathe.

words.tr: v. 颠覆；破坏；使（某人）道德败坏或不忠
words.ex: The rebels subverted the government.
words.ex_cn: v. 叛军颠覆了政府。
words.en: To subvert means to undermine the power and authority of an established system or institution.

words.tr: n. 荞麦粉; 蓼科荞麦属; 荞麦种; 荍
words.ex: Buckwheat is often used in making pancakes.
words.ex_cn: 荞麦常用于制作薄饼。
words.en: Buckwheat is a plant cultivated for its grain-like seeds, and as a cover crop. Despite the name, buckwheat is not related to wheat, as it is not a grass; instead, buckwheat is related to sorrel, knotweed, and rhubarb.

words.ex: Gunpowder was used to make fireworks.
words.ex_cn: 火药被用来制作烟花。
words.en: A black or brown explosive substance consisting of a mixture of potassium nitrate, charcoal, and sulfur, used in gunnery and as a blasting agent in mining.

words.ex: The statesmen met to discuss peace.
words.ex_cn: 这些政治家会面讨论和平。
words.en: A statesman is a respected political leader or figure, especially one who has had a long and successful career in politics and is known for their wisdom and integrity.

words.tr: n. 爆炸；（感情）爆发；激增；
words.ex: The explosion broke all the windows.
words.ex_cn: 爆炸震碎了所有的窗户。
words.en: An explosion is a sudden, violent burst of energy, for example one caused by a bomb.

words.ex: They are disputing over the terms of the contract.
words.ex_cn: 他们正在就合同条款进行争论。
words.en: To argue about something, especially in a formal or legal context.

words.ex: The druggists in the town are very knowledgeable about herbal remedies.
words.ex_cn: 镇上的药剂师对草药疗法非常了解。
words.en: A druggist is a person who is qualified to prepare and sell medicines and drugs.

words.ex: The chemicals are hazardous to health.
words.ex_cn: 这些化学物质对健康有危险。
words.en: Something that is hazardous is dangerous, especially to people's health or safety.

words.tr: n. 变白，白粉 v. （使某物）变白或更白( whiten的现在分词 )
words.ex: The whitening of the teeth can be achieved through various methods.
words.ex_cn: 牙齿的变白可以通过多种方法实现。
words.en: The process of making something white or lighter in color.

words.tr: n. 突然冲入；急速增加
words.ex: The irruption of birds scared the children.
words.ex_cn: 鸟群的突然涌入吓到了孩子们。
words.en: An irruption is a sudden, violent, or forcible entry or invasion.

words.tr: adj. 长满植物的；植被覆盖的
words.ex: The area was densely vegetated, making it difficult to walk through.
words.ex_cn: 这个地区植被茂密，难以穿行。
words.en: Covered with plants or vegetation.

words.tr: adj. 令人吃惊的； v. “startle”的现在分词；
words.ex: The news was startling to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个消息让所有人都感到吃惊。
words.en: Something that is startling is so surprising, unexpected, or remarkable that it makes you feel slightly shocked.

words.ex: The artist besmeared the canvas with vibrant colors.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家用鲜艳的颜色涂抹画布。
words.en: To spread or daub (a substance) over a surface; to soil or stain.

words.tr:
n. 第三十；三十分之一
adj. 第三十的；三十分之一的
adv. 第三十
words.ex: Today is his thirtieth birthday.
words.ex_cn: 今天是他三十岁的生日。
words.en: The thirtieth item in a series is the one that you count as number thirty.

words.tr: v. 评定( assess的现在分词 ); 估价; 对（财产、收入等）进行估价（作为征税根据）; 确
words.ex: The teacher is assessing the students' homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师正在评估学生的作业。
words.en: To assess something means to consider it in order to make a judgment about it.

words.ex: The baby is connected to the mother by an umbilical cord.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿通过脐带与母亲相连。
words.en: relating to or affecting the navel or umbilical cord

words.ex: The teacher will terminate the class at 5 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 老师将在下午5点结束课程。
words.en: To terminate something means to bring it to an end or to stop it from continuing.

words.tr: adj. 不流血的；无伤亡的；无血色的
words.ex: The negotiations were described as bloodless and efficient.
words.ex_cn: 谈判被描述为不流血且高效。
words.en: If you describe someone's face or skin as bloodless, you mean that it is very pale. If you describe an event as bloodless, you mean that it does not involve any violence or any killing.

words.ex: The schoolboy solved the math problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 那个小学生很快解出了这道数学题。
words.en: A schoolboy is a boy who attends school.

words.ex: The subtility of his argument was impressive.
words.ex_cn: n. 他论点的微妙之处令人印象深刻。
words.en: The quality of being subtle; delicacy or complexity of character or meaning.

words.ex: He is impatient when he waits for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他等公交车时很不耐烦。
words.en: If you are impatient, you are easily annoyed by delays or by people making mistakes.

words.ex: The ship foundered in the storm.
words.ex_cn: v. 船在风暴中沉没了。
words.en: If something such as a plan or project founders, it fails because of a particular problem or difficulty.

words.ex: He feared eternal damnation for his sins.
words.ex_cn: 他害怕因为自己的罪过而遭受永恒的诅咒。
words.en: The act of condemning someone to eternal punishment in hell; the state of being condemned in this way.

words.tr: adj. 长满…的； v. “overgrow”的过去分词；
words.ex: The garden is overgrown with weeds.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园长满了杂草。
words.en: If a place is overgrown, it is covered with plants that have grown in an uncontrolled way.

words.ex: The train is departing from platform 3.
words.ex_cn: 火车正在从3号站台出发。
words.en: To leave, especially to start a journey.

words.ex: The teacher instructs the students to complete their homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师指示学生们完成他们的作业。
words.en: To instruct someone means to teach them a subject or skill, or to give them information or orders.

words.tr: v. 使模糊；使难以理解
words.ex: The fog is obscuring the road.
words.ex_cn: 雾正在遮蔽道路。
words.en: To make something unclear or difficult to understand or see.

words.ex: The government imposed sanctions on the company for breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 政府因该公司违法而对其实施了处罚。
words.en: Sanctions are measures taken by a country or an international organization to force another country to obey international law or to punish it for breaking it.

words.ex: She often ruminates on the meaning of life.
words.ex_cn: 她经常思考生命的意义。
words.en: To think deeply about something; to meditate or ponder.

words.ex: He doesn't know his parentage.
words.ex_cn: 他不知道自己的身世。
words.en: The identity or origins of one's parents.

words.tr: adj. 不可言喻的；无法形容的；避讳的
words.ex: The beauty of the sunset was ineffable.
words.ex_cn: 日落的美是无法言喻的。
words.en: If you describe something as ineffable, you mean that it is so impressive or extreme that it cannot be described in words.

words.tr: adj. 分成方格的； v. “checker”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The table has a checkered cloth.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子上有块方格布。
words.en: Something that is checkered has a pattern of squares, usually of two different colors, or has had a lot of different experiences or events, often both good and bad.

words.tr: n. 提取器；排气扇；抽油烟机；抽出器
words.ex: The extractor removes oil from the machine.
words.ex_cn: extractor 从机器中去除油。
words.en: An extractor is a device or machine that is used to remove something from something else, especially by using force or suction.

words.tr: adj. 可航行的；适于通航的；
words.ex: The river is navigable by small boats.
words.ex_cn: 这条河可供小船航行。
words.en: If a stretch of water is navigable, it is deep and wide enough for ships to travel through.

words.tr: n. 陈词滥调；老生常谈；
words.ex: His speech was full of platitudes about hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了关于努力工作的陈词滥调。
words.en: A platitude is a statement that has been used so often that it is meaningless and shows a lack of original thought.

words.tr: v. 获胜；获胜( triumph的过去式和过去分词 )；
words.ex: He triumphed in the final match.
words.ex_cn: 他在决赛中获胜。
words.en: To achieve a victory; to be successful.

words.tr: n. 恐怖主义；恐怖行动
words.ex: The country is fighting terrorism with strong laws.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家通过严格的法律打击恐怖主义。
words.en: Terrorism is the use of violence and intimidation in the pursuit of political aims.

words.ex: The weather was inclement, so we stayed home.
words.ex_cn: 天气恶劣，所以我们待在家里。
words.en: (of weather) unpleasantly cold or wet.

words.ex: She dedicates her life to helping the poor.
words.ex_cn: 她致力于帮助穷人。
words.en: To dedicate means to devote time, effort, or oneself to a particular task or purpose.

words.ex: The teacher chastised the boy for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他在课堂上说话而责骂了他。
words.en: to criticize someone severely or punish them in order to correct their behavior

words.tr:
n. 编年史；年代记
v. 按时间顺序记录
words.ex: He writes a chronicle of his daily life.
words.ex_cn: 他记录自己每天的生活。
words.en: A chronicle is a historical account of events arranged in chronological order, typically without analysis or interpretation.

words.tr:
adj. 腐蚀性的；起破坏作用的
n. 腐蚀性物品
words.ex: The acid is corrosive and can damage metal.
words.ex_cn: 这种酸具有腐蚀性，会损坏金属。
words.en: A corrosive substance is able to destroy solid materials by a chemical reaction.

words.ex: The musicians played songs at the park.
words.ex_cn: 音乐家们在公园里演奏歌曲。
words.en: A musician is a person who plays a musical instrument as their job or hobby.

words.tr: adv. 悲惨地；不幸地；糟糕地
words.ex: He slept miserably after the fight.
words.ex_cn: 打架后，他睡得很不舒服。
words.en: In a manner that is extremely unhappy or uncomfortable; very badly.

words.ex: Too much alcohol is impairing his judgment.
words.ex_cn: 过多的酒精正在削弱他的判断力。
words.en: If something impairs something such as an ability or the way something works, it damages it or makes it worse.

words.ex: He has a small birthmark on his arm.
words.ex_cn: 他的手臂上有一个小胎记。
words.en: A birthmark is a mark on the skin that is present at birth or appears shortly after birth.

words.ex: His indolence at work was becoming a serious issue.
words.ex_cn: 他在工作中的懒散正成为一个严重的问题。
words.en: Indolence is the state of being lazy or not wanting to do any work.

words.ex: She is objecting to the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 她正在反对新政策。
words.en: To express or feel disapproval, resistance, or dislike towards something.

words.ex: He used various artifices to deceive his opponents.
words.ex_cn: 他使用了各种诡计来欺骗他的对手。
words.en: Clever or cunning devices or expedients, especially as used to trick or deceive others.

words.tr: n. 计件工作；按件计酬的工作
words.ex: He gets paid by piecework, earning $5 for each item he makes.
words.ex_cn: 他按计件工资领取报酬，每制作一个物品赚5美元。
words.en: Piecework is a type of employment in which workers are paid according to the number of items they produce, rather than the amount of time they spend working.

words.ex: She bought a fresh croissant from the bakery.
words.ex_cn: 她从面包店买了一个新鲜羊角面包。
words.en: A croissant is a type of buttery, flaky, viennoiserie pastry of Austrian origin, named for its historical crescent shape.

words.tr: adj. 使人烦恼的；令人恼火的
words.ex: The vexatious lawsuit wasted everyone's time.
words.ex_cn: 这个烦人的诉讼浪费了所有人的时间。
words.en: Causing or tending to cause annoyance, frustration, or worry.

words.tr: n. 饱食；饱满；饱享；厌腻
words.ex: The satiation of hunger made him feel calm.
words.ex_cn: 饥饿的满足让他感到平静。
words.en: The state of being satiated; fullness beyond desire or need, especially with food or pleasure.

words.ex: The reception at the hotel was very friendly.
words.ex_cn: 酒店的接待非常友好。
words.en: The act of receiving or being received, especially in a formal or official context.

words.ex: The sailor fell overboard during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 水手在风暴中从船上掉入海中。
words.en: If someone falls overboard, they fall from a ship into the water. It can also mean doing something to an excessive degree.

words.tr: adj. 可归因于的；可参考的
words.ex: The success of the project is referable to the team's hard work.
words.ex_cn: adj. 项目的成功可归因于团队的辛勤工作。
words.en: Capable of being referred or attributed to something.

words.tr: v. 恢复; 取回( retrieve的过去式和过去分词 ); 寻回; 检索（储存的信息）
words.ex: The data was successfully retrieved from the damaged disk.
words.ex_cn: 数据成功地从损坏的磁盘中恢复了。
words.en: To get something back that was lost or taken away.

words.ex: The heavy traffic is retarding our progress.
words.ex_cn: v. 交通拥堵正在阻碍我们的进展。
words.en: To cause to move or proceed slowly; delay or impede progress.

words.ex: The fabricant specializes in producing high-quality textiles.
words.ex_cn: n. 这家制造商专门生产高质量的纺织品。
words.en: A fabricant is a person or company that manufactures something, especially on a large scale.

words.ex: He received the sacrament on Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他在周日领受了圣礼。
words.en: A sacrament is a Christian religious ceremony or ritual regarded as imparting divine grace, such as baptism, the Eucharist, and (in the Roman Catholic and many Orthodox Churches) penance and anointing of the sick.

words.tr: n. 折磨者；使人痛苦的人或物
words.ex: He was the tormentor of his little brother.
words.ex_cn: 他是他弟弟的折磨者。
words.en: A tormentor is someone who causes great physical or mental suffering to others.

words.ex: He overdosed on painkillers and had to be rushed to the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他过量服用了止痛药，不得不被紧急送往医院。
words.en: To take an excessive and dangerous amount of a drug or medication.

words.ex: The product conformed to all safety standards.
words.ex_cn: 该产品符合所有安全标准。
words.en: To conform means to comply with rules, standards, or laws, or to behave according to socially acceptable conventions or standards.

words.tr: v. 使混乱，扰乱；使混乱，扰乱( disrupt的过去式和过去分词 )；
words.ex: The storm disrupted the train schedule.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴扰乱了火车时刻表。
words.en: If someone or something disrupts an event, system, or process, they cause difficulties that prevent it from continuing or operating in a normal way.

words.tr: n. 一种苏格兰帽，通常为羊毛制成，前面有丝带装饰。
words.ex: He wore a traditional glengarry to the Scottish festival.
words.ex_cn: 他在苏格兰节日上戴了一顶传统的格伦加里帽。
words.en: A glengarry is a traditional Scottish cap made of wool, typically with a ribbon at the front.

words.ex: Botanists study plants in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 植物学家在森林里研究植物。
words.en: A botanist is a scientist who studies plants, including their physiology, structure, genetics, ecology, distribution, classification, and economic importance.

words.ex: He felt sad after the rejection.
words.ex_cn: 在遭到拒绝后，他感到很难过。
words.en: The act of refusing to accept, believe in, or agree with something.

words.tr: adj. 三倍的；三重的；有三部分的；
words.ex: The population has grown threefold in ten years.
words.ex_cn: 十年来，人口增长了三倍。
words.en: Three times as great or as numerous.

words.ex: The boat got stuck on the sandbanks near the coast.
words.ex_cn: 船在海岸附近的沙洲上搁浅了。
words.en: Sandbanks are areas of sand that have been deposited by water, often forming a ridge or mound in a river, lake, or sea.

words.ex: The fallen tree obstructs the road.
words.ex_cn: v. 倒下的树阻碍了道路。
words.en: To block or get in the way of something or someone, preventing movement or progress.

words.ex: The treasurer keeps the club's money safe.
words.ex_cn: 司库保管俱乐部的钱。
words.en: A treasurer is an official who is responsible for the money and accounts of an organization.

words.ex: The onslaught of rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 大量倾泻的雨水淹没了街道。
words.en: An onslaught is a very powerful, often violent, attack against someone or something.

words.tr: adv. 好奇地；奇异地；奇怪地
words.ex: He looked curiously at the strange box.
words.ex_cn: 他好奇地看着那个奇怪的盒子。
words.en: In a way that shows eagerness to know or learn something.

words.ex: The hotel provides lodgement for travelers.
words.ex_cn: 这家酒店为旅行者提供住宿。
words.en: The act of lodging or the state of being lodged; a place where someone or something is lodged.

words.ex: He is inventing a new machine.
words.ex_cn: 他正在发明一台新机器。
words.en: To invent means to create or design something that has not existed before, or to make up a story or excuse.

words.ex: He loves watching stars and learning astronomy.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢看星星并学习天文学。
words.en: Astronomy is the scientific study of celestial objects, space, and the physical universe as a whole.

words.ex: She coquetted with him at the party, making him blush.
words.ex_cn: v. 她在聚会上与他调情，让他脸红了。
words.en: To behave in a flirtatious manner; to act in a way that is intended to attract attention or admiration.

words.ex: The two paintings are semblable in style.
words.ex_cn: 这两幅画在风格上相似。
words.en: Similar or alike in appearance or nature.

words.tr: adj. 不知道的；没察觉的
words.ex: She remained unknowing of the truth until it was too late.
words.ex_cn: 她直到为时已晚才得知真相。
words.en: If you describe someone as unknowing, you mean that they are not aware of what is happening or of what they are doing.

words.ex: The remote needs new batteries.
words.ex_cn: 这个遥控器需要新电池。
words.en: Batteries are devices that store energy and convert it into electricity, used to power various devices.

words.tr: adj. 讨厌的；可恶的；令人憎恶的
words.ex: The smell of the rotten food was loathsome.
words.ex_cn: 腐烂食物的气味令人作呕。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as loathsome, you are indicating that they are extremely unpleasant and disgusting.

words.tr:
adj. 开玩笑的；风趣的；诙谐的
v. 轻松说笑；“banter”的现在分词
words.ex: His bantering tone made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他风趣的语气让每个人都笑了。
words.en: Bantering refers to the act of exchanging light, playful, teasing remarks.

words.ex: The apple will decompose in the soil.
words.ex_cn: 苹果会在土壤中分解。
words.en: If something decomposes, or if it is decomposed, it decays or breaks down into smaller parts or substances.

words.tr: v. 趾高气扬地走；炫耀
words.ex: He was strutting around the office like he owned the place.
words.ex_cn: 他在办公室里趾高气扬地走来走去，好像他是那里的主人。
words.en: walking with a proud, confident, and often arrogant or pompous gait.

words.tr: n. 乐观主义者( optimist的名词复数 )
words.ex: Optimists believe good things will happen.
words.ex_cn: 乐观者相信好事会发生。
words.en: Optimists are people who always expect good things to happen or who believe that the future will be better than the present.

words.ex: His judgments about people are often fair.
words.ex_cn: 他对人的判断通常很公正。
words.en: The ability to make considered decisions or come to sensible conclusions.

words.tr: adj. 和平的；平静的；温顺的
words.ex: The two neighbors are peaceable and never argue.
words.ex_cn: 这两个邻居很和睦，从不争吵。
words.en: A peaceable person or society is one that avoids violence or conflict and tries to live in a calm and peaceful way.

words.tr:
n. 蒙古人；蒙古国民；蒙古语
adj. 蒙古的；蒙古人的；蒙古语的
words.ex: He is from Mongolia and speaks Mongolian.
words.ex_cn: 他来自蒙古，会说蒙古语。
words.en: Of or relating to Mongolia, its people, or their language.

words.tr: adj. 适合刊印的；可印刷的
words.ex: The document is printable and ready for distribution.
words.ex_cn: 该文件可打印并准备分发。
words.en: Capable of being printed or published; suitable for printing.

words.ex: The plaintiff sued the company for damages.
words.ex_cn: 原告起诉该公司要求赔偿。
words.en: A plaintiff is a person who brings a case against another in a court of law.

words.ex: The mirror had several blemishes on its surface.
words.ex_cn: 镜子的表面有几个瑕疵。
words.en: Blemishes are small marks or flaws that spoil the appearance of something.

words.tr: adj. 使疲倦的；令人厌烦的；乏味的
words.ex: The wearisome task of filling out forms took hours.
words.ex_cn: 填写表格这项乏味的任务花了好几个小时。
words.en: If you describe something as wearisome, you mean that it is very tiring and boring or frustrating.

words.ex: The teacher keeps extra books in the storeroom.
words.ex_cn: 老师把多余的书放在贮藏室里。
words.en: A room or area where items are stored.

words.tr: adj. 明智的；有见识的；判断正确的
words.ex: He made a judicious choice about which book to buy.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个明智的买书决定。
words.en: If you describe an action or decision as judicious, you approve of it because you think that it shows good judgment and sense.

words.ex: Drugs can alleviate pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To make something less severe or intense.

words.tr:
adj. 受压抑的；受抑制的
v. 抑制；压抑；镇压；“repress”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She had a repressed personality, always keeping her emotions in check.
words.ex_cn: 她性格压抑，总是克制自己的情感。
words.en: If someone is repressed, they are prevented from expressing their feelings or desires, often because of social rules or fear.

words.tr: n.  浮华；虚夸；炫耀；自负
words.ex: His pomposity often alienated his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他的自大使他经常疏远同事。
words.en: Pomposity is the quality of being pompous; self-importance.

words.ex: The bridge can withstand strong winds.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥能经受住强风。
words.en: If something or someone withstands a force or action, they survive it or do not give in to it.

words.tr: v. 滋养；养育；怀有（希望等）
words.ex: A good diet nourishes the body and the mind.
words.ex_cn: 良好的饮食滋养身体和心灵。
words.en: To nourish means to provide with the food or other substances necessary for growth, health, and good condition. It can also mean to keep a feeling or belief strong or in existence.

words.ex: Epidemics can spread quickly in crowded cities.
words.ex_cn: 流行病在拥挤的城市中可能迅速传播。
words.en: Epidemics refer to the rapid spread of infectious diseases to a large number of people in a given population within a short period of time.

words.ex: The teacher is imparting knowledge to her students.
words.ex_cn: 老师正在向她的学生传授知识。
words.en: To impart means to give, convey, or communicate something, such as knowledge, information, or a quality, to someone.

words.ex: He has seventeen apples in his basket.
words.ex_cn: 他的篮子里有十七个苹果。
words.en: The number seventeen is the natural number following sixteen and preceding eighteen.

words.ex: The signalman ensured the train passed safely through the junction.
words.ex_cn: 信号员确保火车安全通过交叉口。
words.en: A signalman is a person responsible for operating signals, especially on a railway or in the military, to ensure the safe passage of trains or the transmission of messages.

words.ex: The rocket propelled into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 火箭被推入了天空。
words.en: To propel something means to push or drive it forward.

words.ex: The washerman comes to our house every Monday to collect the dirty clothes.
words.ex_cn: n. 洗衣工每周一来我们家收脏衣服。
words.en: A washerman is a man whose job is to wash clothes, especially as an occupation.

words.ex: Paraffins are commonly used in candle making.
words.ex_cn: 石蜡常用于制作蜡烛。
words.en: Paraffins are a group of aliphatic hydrocarbons with the general formula CnH2n+2, commonly found in petroleum and used in various applications such as candle making and lubrication.

words.ex: The upholders of the law ensured justice was served.
words.ex_cn: n. 法律的维护者确保正义得到伸张。
words.en: People who support or maintain a particular principle or law.

words.tr: n. 出租房屋；经济公寓
words.ex: The city has many old tenements that are in need of repair.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市有许多需要维修的老旧出租房屋。
words.en: A tenement is a large building divided into apartments, usually in a poor area of a city.

words.ex: He proffered his help to the stranded travelers.
words.ex_cn: v. 他向被困的旅行者提供了帮助。
words.en: If you proffer something to someone, you offer it to them for them to accept or reject.

words.ex: The teacher was extolling the virtues of hard work to her students.
words.ex_cn: 老师向学生们颂扬努力工作的美德。
words.en: If you extol something or someone, you praise them enthusiastically.

words.tr: adv. 故意地；有目的地；特意地；
words.ex: He purposely broke the vase to get attention.
words.ex_cn: 他故意打碎了花瓶以引起注意。
words.en: If you do something purposely, you do it intentionally.

words.ex: Applications arrived in an avalanche after the job posting.
words.ex_cn: 职位发布后，申请纷至沓来。
words.en: An avalanche is a large mass of snow, ice, and rocks that falls quickly down the side of a mountain.

words.tr: adj. 富有的( wealthy的比较级 )
words.ex: He is wealthier than his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他比他兄弟更富有。
words.en: Having more wealth or resources than someone or something else.

words.ex: The book was full of misprints, which made it difficult to read.
words.ex_cn: 这本书充满了印刷错误，使得阅读变得困难。
words.en: Misprints are errors in printed text, such as incorrect words, letters, or punctuation.

words.tr: v. 加深；加强；恶化；“deepen”的现在分词
words.ex: The deepening shadows of the evening made it difficult to see.
words.ex_cn: 傍晚渐深的阴影使得视线变得困难。
words.en: If a situation or emotion deepens or if something deepens it, it becomes stronger and more intense.

words.ex: The mistake was glaringly obvious.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误非常明显。
words.en: In a way that is very obvious or conspicuous.

words.ex: Her words were prompting him to try again.
words.ex_cn: 她的话激励他再次尝试。
words.en: The action of saying something to persuade, encourage, or remind someone to do or say something.

words.ex: He knows good etiquette at dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他知道晚餐时的礼貌规矩。
words.en: Etiquette refers to the customary code of polite behavior in society or among members of a particular profession or group.

words.tr: adj. 典范的；可做模范的；惩戒性的
words.ex: He is an exemplary student who always finishes his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名模范学生，总是完成作业。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as exemplary, you think they are extremely good and suitable to be copied by other people.

words.ex: He receives monthly annuities from his retirement plan.
words.ex_cn: n. 他从退休计划中每月领取年金。
words.en: An annuity is a fixed sum of money paid to someone each year, typically for the rest of their life.

words.tr: adj. 莽撞的；有勇无谋的
words.ex: He made a foolhardy decision to climb the mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个有勇无谋的决定，独自去爬山。
words.en: If you describe behavior or an action as foolhardy, you mean that it is very risky because it shows a lack of thought or care for the possible consequences.

words.tr: n. 巡回者；巡警；送报员
words.ex: The roundsmen deliver newspapers to every house in the neighborhood.
words.ex_cn: 送报员将报纸送到社区的每一户人家。
words.en: A roundsman is a person who makes regular visits to a particular area, such as a police officer patrolling a beat or a delivery person who delivers goods to homes or businesses.

words.ex: He is diffident when he speaks in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他在全班面前说话时很腼腆。
words.en: If you are diffident, you are rather shy and do not enjoy talking about yourself or being noticed by other people.

words.ex: She surmounts every obstacle with determination.
words.ex_cn: 她以决心克服每一个障碍。
words.en: To surmount means to overcome a difficulty or obstacle, or to get to the top of something.

words.ex: The product was promoted by several famous endorsers.
words.ex_cn: 该产品由几位著名的背书人推广。
words.en: People or organizations that publicly support or recommend a product, service, or idea.

words.ex: It is advisable to wear a helmet when riding a bike.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是明智的。
words.en: If something is advisable, it will avoid problems if you do it.

words.ex: The aftermath of the storm left many trees down.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，许多树被吹倒了。
words.en: The aftermath of an important event, especially a harmful one, is the situation that results from it.

words.ex: He never derogates his colleagues in public.
words.ex_cn: 他从不公开贬低他的同事。
words.en: To detract from the authority, dignity, or reputation of someone or something.

words.tr: v. 解开；分离；使解脱；脱离战斗
words.ex: He tried to disengage from the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他试图从争论中抽身。
words.en: To disengage means to separate or detach oneself from something or someone, or to release from a connection or obligation.

words.ex: The thickness of the ice is dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 冰的厚度很危险。
words.en: The quality or state of being thick, especially the distance between opposite surfaces of an object.

words.ex: She planted marigolds in her garden to add a splash of color.
words.ex_cn: 她在花园里种了金盏花，增添了一抹色彩。
words.en: Marigolds are a type of flowering plant known for their bright yellow or orange flowers, often used in gardens and traditional medicine.

words.tr: v. 把…视为名人；过分吹捧
words.ex: The media has been lionising the young athlete for his recent achievements.
words.ex_cn: 媒体一直在过分吹捧这位年轻运动员最近的成就。
words.en: To treat someone as a celebrity or to praise them excessively.

words.ex: The sharpness of the knife cut the apple easily.
words.ex_cn: 刀的锋利很容易地切开了苹果。
words.en: The quality of being able to cut or pierce easily; the quality of being keenly perceptive or intelligent.

words.ex: He is an assiduous student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤奋的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is assiduous works hard or does things very thoroughly.

words.ex: The university received a large endowment from a philanthropist.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学收到了一位慈善家的大量捐赠。
words.en: An endowment is a gift of money that is made to an institution or community in order to provide it with an annual income.

words.ex: We celebrate my birthday with cake and friends.
words.ex_cn: 我们用蛋糕和朋友庆祝我的生日。
words.en: To celebrate means to mark a special day, event, or occasion with festivities or ceremonies. It can also mean to praise or honor someone or something.

words.ex: She forwarded the email to her colleague.
words.ex_cn: v. 她把邮件转发给了她的同事。
words.en: To send something on to a further destination.

words.ex: She looked at him cynically and shook her head.
words.ex_cn: 她冷笑着看着他，摇了摇头。
words.en: In a manner that is distrustful of human sincerity or integrity.

words.ex: The new policy furthered the development of renewable energy.
words.ex_cn: 新政策促进了可再生能源的发展。
words.en: To help the progress or development of something; to promote.

words.tr: n. 食人者；同类相食的动物
words.ex: The explorers were warned about the cannibals in the jungle.
words.ex_cn: 探险者们被警告丛林中有食人族。
words.en: Cannibals are people who eat the flesh of other human beings.

words.ex: He was thirsting for adventure in the vast wilderness.
words.ex_cn: 他渴望在广阔的荒野中冒险。
words.en: Having a strong desire for something.

words.tr: n. 热烈；强烈；猛烈；愤怒
words.ex: He spoke with vehemence about the injustice.
words.ex_cn: 他充满激情地谈论着不公。
words.en: Vehemence is the display of strong feeling; passion.

words.ex: The long exposures to the sun can damage your skin.
words.ex_cn: 长时间暴露在阳光下会损害你的皮肤。
words.en: The state of being exposed to something, especially to the elements or to a particular influence.

words.ex: The restaurant is a favorite among gourmands.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅是美食家的最爱。
words.en: A gourmand is a person who enjoys eating and often eats too much.

words.tr: v. 评价； adj. 估价的，已评估的 v. 评价( evaluate的过去式和过去分词 )；
words.ex: The teacher evaluated his homework carefully.
words.ex_cn: 老师仔细评价了他的作业。
words.en: If you evaluate something or someone, you consider them in order to make a judgment about them, for example about how good or bad they are.

words.ex: The guard showed vigilance during the night shift.
words.ex_cn: 守卫在夜班期间保持警惕。
words.en: Vigilance is the action or state of keeping careful watch for possible danger or difficulties.

words.ex: The small town blossomed after the new factory opened.
words.ex_cn: 这家新工厂开业后，这个小镇繁荣了起来。
words.en: To produce flowers; to develop or grow in a promising or healthy way.

words.tr: n. 脆弱性；脆性；易碎性
words.ex: The fragility of the glass made it easy to break.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃的易碎性让它很容易破碎。
words.en: The quality of being easily broken or damaged.

words.tr:
adj. 特许的；（船等）租的
v. 包租（汽车、飞机等）；“charter”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is a chartered accountant with extensive experience.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位经验丰富的特许会计师。
words.en: If a vehicle such as a bus, aircraft, or boat is chartered, it is rented for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The company reported large surpluses this quarter.
words.ex_cn: 该公司本季度报告了巨额盈余。
words.en: Surpluses refer to an amount of something left over when requirements have been met; an excess of production or supply over demand.

words.tr: n. 集合；合流；群众；中央大厅；车站广场
words.ex: The concourse of people filled the square.
words.ex_cn: 人群集合在广场上。
words.en: A concourse is a large open area inside or in front of a public building, such as a station or an airport, where people can meet or wait.

words.tr: adj. 无害的；无冒犯之意的
words.ex: The comment was innocuous and didn't upset anyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个评论无害，没有惹恼任何人。
words.en: Something that is innocuous is not harmful or offensive.

words.tr: n. 完成者；终结者；最后加工者
words.ex: The finishers of the marathon received medals for their achievement.
words.ex_cn: 马拉松的完成者因为他们的成就获得了奖牌。
words.en: Finishers are people or things that complete a task or process, especially the final stages of a project or competition.

words.tr: adj. 权宜的；临时凑合的；
words.ex: He used a makeshift table made of boxes and a board.
words.ex_cn: 他用箱子和木板做了一个权宜的桌子。
words.en: A makeshift object or arrangement is one that is made or done quickly and without much skill, using whatever is available at the time.

words.ex: She is regaining her strength after the illness.
words.ex_cn: 她在病后正在恢复体力。
words.en: To get back something that you had before.

words.ex: He is tinkering with his old radio.
words.ex_cn: 他正在摆弄他的旧收音机。
words.en: To tinker means to make small changes to something in an attempt to repair or improve it.

words.ex: The biologist dissected the frog to study its internal organs.
words.ex_cn: 生物学家解剖了青蛙以研究其内部器官。
words.en: To dissect means to cut apart or separate (tissue) for anatomical study, or to analyze and interpret minutely.

words.ex: He felt antipathy toward the loud neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对那个吵闹的邻居感到反感。
words.en: A deep-seated feeling of dislike; aversion.

words.tr: n. 营养品；养料；营养的来源；食物
words.ex: Food provides nutriment for the body.
words.ex_cn: 食物为身体提供营养。
words.en: Nutriment refers to substances that provide nourishment essential for the maintenance of life and for growth.

words.ex: Green trees surrounds the small house.
words.ex_cn: 绿色的树木环绕着这所小房子。
words.en: To be all around something or someone, often in a way that encloses or encircles them.

words.ex: They tried to extirpate the weeds from the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图把花园里的杂草彻底清除。
words.en: To destroy or remove something completely, especially a problem or an organization.

words.tr:
adj. 有溶解力的；消散的
n. 溶剂；解决方案
words.ex: The resolvent liquid dissolves sugar quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种有溶解力的液体能快速溶解糖。
words.en: A resolvent is a substance that has the ability to dissolve other substances, or it can refer to something that resolves a problem or dispute.

words.ex: He bought apples, oranges, etceteras.
words.ex_cn: 他买了苹果、橙子和其他东西。
words.en: Used at the end of a list to indicate that further, similar items are included.

words.tr: n. 主考者( examiner的名词复数 )
words.ex: The examiners were impressed by the students' performance.
words.ex_cn: 考官们对学生们的表现印象深刻。
words.en: People who conduct formal assessments or tests.

words.ex: Exercise is enhancing his strength.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼正在增强他的力量。
words.en: To enhance something means to improve its value, quality, or attractiveness.

words.ex: The teacher gave each student two copybooks for writing practice.
words.ex_cn: 老师给每个学生发了两本练习本用于写字练习。
words.en: A copybook is a book in which students practice writing by copying examples.

words.ex: The city manages water and electricity utilities.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市管理供水和电力等公用事业。
words.en: Utilities refer to services provided for the public, such as electricity, gas, and water, or software tools designed to perform specific tasks.

words.ex: The authoress signed copies of her latest novel at the bookstore.
words.ex_cn: n. 这位女作家在书店为她最新的小说签名。
words.en: A female author.

words.tr: v. 慷慨地给予；大量地使用
words.ex: She was lavishing gifts on her grandchildren.
words.ex_cn: 她慷慨地给她的孙子孙女们送礼物。
words.en: To give or spend in large amounts; to bestow something in generous or extravagant quantities.

words.tr: n. 格林尼治（英国伦敦东南部一区，位于泰晤士河南岸，为地球经度起算点）；
words.ex: The Royal Observatory is in Greenwich.
words.ex_cn: 皇家天文台位于格林尼治。
words.en: Greenwich is a district of London, England, notable for its maritime history and for giving its name to the Greenwich Meridian (0° longitude) and Greenwich Mean Time.

words.ex: She is known for her spirituel remarks at social gatherings.
words.ex_cn: 她在社交聚会上以机智的言辞而闻名。
words.en: Witty and clever, often in a sophisticated or intellectual way.

words.tr:
n. 阿根廷人
adj. 阿根廷的；阿根廷人的
words.ex: The Argentine team won the World Cup.
words.ex_cn: 阿根廷队赢得了世界杯。
words.en: Of or relating to Argentina or its people; resembling silver; silvery.

words.tr:
n. 渴望；期望
v. 渴望；追求；“hanker”的现在分词
words.ex: He had a hankering for adventure.
words.ex_cn: 他对冒险有着强烈的渴望。
words.en: A hankering is a strong feeling of wanting something.

words.ex: The cats are sitting on the housetops and looking around.
words.ex_cn: 猫坐在房顶上四处张望。
words.en: The plural form of 'housetop', referring to the roofs of houses.

words.tr: n. 附庸地位；臣属关系
words.ex: The small kingdom was in vassalage to the larger empire.
words.ex_cn: 这个小王国是那个大帝国的附庸。
words.en: The state of being a vassal or the obligations of a vassal to a lord.

words.tr: adj. 证明有罪的；已被判刑的；
words.ex: He was convicted of stealing money.
words.ex_cn: 他被证明有罪，因偷钱而定罪。
words.en: If someone is convicted of a crime, they are found guilty of that crime in a law court.

words.ex: He tried to integrate into the new school community.
words.ex_cn: 他试图融入新的学校群体。
words.en: If someone integrates into a social group, or is integrated into it, they behave in such a way that they become part of the group or are accepted into it.

words.ex: The managers met in the boardroom to discuss the plan.
words.ex_cn: 经理们在会议室里讨论计划。
words.en: A boardroom is a room where the board of directors of a company meets.

words.ex: The story is a tentation of the hero's moral integrity.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事是对英雄道德完整性的试探。
words.en: The act of testing or trying something, especially to see how it works or how people react to it.

words.ex: The doctor drained the abscesses to relieve the patient's pain.
words.ex_cn: 医生排出了脓肿以减轻病人的疼痛。
words.en: An abscess is a swollen area within body tissue, containing an accumulation of pus.

words.ex: She was remarking on the beautiful scenery.
words.ex_cn: 她正在评论美丽的风景。
words.en: To say something as a comment; to notice or observe something.

words.tr: adj. 散漫的；不连贯的；断续的
words.ex: He gave a desultory answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个漫无目的的回答。
words.en: Something that is desultory is done in an unplanned and disorganized way, and without enthusiasm.

words.ex: The intricacy of the clock made it very special.
words.ex_cn: 这座钟的复杂精细让它非常特别。
words.en: The quality of being intricate; complexity.

words.ex: The pigs were wallowing in the mud.
words.ex_cn: v. 猪在泥浆中打滚。
words.en: To roll about or lie in water, mud, dust, etc., especially for pleasure; to indulge in an unrestrained way in something that creates a pleasurable sensation.

words.ex: The old oak tree in the curtilage provides shade during the summer.
words.ex_cn: n. 庭院里的老橡树在夏天提供了阴凉。
words.en: The area of land attached to a house and forming one enclosure with it.

words.ex: The new policy is affording more opportunities for young entrepreneurs.
words.ex_cn: 新政策为年轻企业家提供了更多机会。
words.en: If you can afford something, you have enough money to buy it or enough time to do it.

words.tr: n. 煽动者；蛊惑民心的政客
words.ex: The politician is a demagogue who uses angry words to win votes.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客是一个煽动者，用愤怒的言辞赢得选票。
words.en: A demagogue is a political leader who seeks support by appealing to popular desires and prejudices rather than by using rational argument.

words.ex: The museum has a special exhibit on orientals.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆有一个关于东方文化的特别展览。
words.en: People or things from the East, especially East Asia, or relating to the culture of East Asia.

words.ex: He agreed agreeably to the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他愉快地同意了这个计划。
words.en: In a pleasant or enjoyable manner.

words.tr: n. 月光; 空谈; 私酒; 妄想
words.ex: The old man used to talk about the moonshine in the countryside.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人过去常常谈论乡下的月光。
words.en: Moonshine is a clear, strong alcoholic drink, typically whiskey, that is made illegally.

words.tr: n.  不关心；不感兴趣；冷漠
words.ex: He showed unconcern about the exam results.
words.ex_cn: 他对考试成绩毫不关心。
words.en: If you have a feeling of unconcern, you are not worried or anxious about something, often because you do not care about it or do not think it is important.

words.ex: The author has rewritten the ending of the novel to make it more dramatic.
words.ex_cn: 作者重写了小说的结尾，使其更具戏剧性。
words.en: To write something again in a different way, usually in order to improve it or to change its meaning.

words.ex: The potencies of these herbs are well-documented in traditional medicine.
words.ex_cn: 这些草药在传统医学中的效力有详细记载。
words.en: The inherent capacity or power to produce effects or results.

words.ex: The acceptors of the award were very grateful.
words.ex_cn: n. 奖项的接受者非常感激。
words.en: Acceptors are individuals or entities that receive something, such as an award or a role in a process. In electronics, acceptors refer to atoms that accept electrons in semiconductor materials.

words.tr: adj. 恶毒的；恶性的；恶意的
words.ex: His malignant words hurt everyone around him.
words.ex_cn: 他恶毒的话语伤害了周围的所有人。
words.en: If you say that someone is malignant, you mean they are very dangerous and cause harm to people.

words.ex: The teacher emphasise the importance of homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调了作业的重要性。
words.en: To emphasise something means to indicate that it is particularly important or true, or to draw special attention to it.

words.tr: adj. 可笑的；荒谬的；滑稽的
words.ex: It is ludicrous to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套真是荒谬。
words.en: If you describe something as ludicrous, you are emphasizing that you think it is foolish, unreasonable, or unsuitable.

words.ex: He is conveying a message to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他正在向朋友传达一条信息。
words.en: To convey means to communicate or make known; to transport or carry from one place to another; to transfer or deliver (something, such as property) to another especially by a sealed writing.

words.tr: adj. 最外面的；（离中心）最远的
words.ex: The outermost layer of the onion is brown.
words.ex_cn: 洋葱最外层是棕色的。
words.en: situated at the farthest possible point from the center

words.tr: adj. 紧握的；顽强的；坚决的；强的（记忆力）
words.ex: The child held the toy with tenacious hands.
words.ex_cn: 孩子用紧握的手抓住玩具。
words.en: If you describe someone as tenacious, you are admiring their determination to do something and their refusal to stop trying even when it is difficult.

words.ex: The constable stopped the car for speeding.
words.ex_cn: 警察因超速拦下了那辆车。
words.en: A constable is a police officer of the lowest rank, especially in a town or village.

words.tr: n. 计算机操作；计算； v. “compute”的现在分词；
words.ex: Computing helps us solve math problems quickly.
words.ex_cn: 计算机操作帮助我们快速解决数学问题。
words.en: Computing is the activity of using computers and writing programs for them.

words.ex: The king was dethroned after a long and bloody revolution.
words.ex_cn: v. 国王在一场漫长而血腥的革命后被废黜了。
words.en: To remove a monarch or leader from power, especially by force.

words.ex: The inquirers were eager to learn more about the ancient ruins.
words.ex_cn: 询问者们渴望了解更多关于古代遗迹的信息。
words.en: People who ask questions or seek information.

words.ex: The clown entertains the children with funny tricks.
words.ex_cn: 小丑用滑稽的把戏娱乐孩子们。
words.en: To entertain someone means to amuse or interest them, for example by telling them stories or jokes, or by playing music for them.

words.ex: The machinist fixes machines in the factory.
words.ex_cn: 这位机械师在工厂修理机器。
words.en: A machinist is a person who operates or maintains machines, especially in a factory or workshop.

words.ex: The tightness of the bottle cap prevents leaks.
words.ex_cn: 瓶盖的紧密性防止了泄漏。
words.en: The quality or condition of being tight.

words.ex: He drew a simple schematic of the circuit.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一个电路的简单示意图。
words.en: A schematic diagram or representation is a simple drawing that uses symbols to show the parts of something and how they are connected.

words.tr: n. 冒充内行者；庸医；骗子
words.ex: He is a charlatan who pretends to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他是个冒充医生的骗子。
words.en: A charlatan is someone who pretends to have skills or knowledge that they do not really possess.

words.ex: He wanted vengeance after his brother was hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他哥哥被伤害后，他想要报复。
words.en: Vengeance is the act of doing something harmful or unpleasant to someone because they have done something harmful or unpleasant to you.

words.ex: The garden was filled with the songs of throstles.
words.ex_cn: 花园里充满了画眉鸟的歌声。
words.en: Throstles are small songbirds known for their melodious singing.

words.tr: v. （使马）飞奔； adj. 急性的；飞驰的，急性的 v. （使马）飞奔，奔驰( gallop的现在分词 )；
words.ex: The boy was galloping his horse across the field.
words.ex_cn: 男孩正骑着马在田野上飞奔。
words.en: Galloping is used to describe something that is moving or developing very quickly.

words.ex: The painting has a simple aesthetic appeal.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有一种简单的审美吸引力。
words.en: Concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty.

words.ex: They live on the outskirts of the city.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在城市的郊区。
words.en: The outskirts of a city or town are the parts of it that are farthest away from its center.

words.tr: v. 重新充电；使恢复精力
words.ex: He recharged his phone before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前给手机充了电。
words.en: To restore energy or power to something, especially a battery, or to regain energy or enthusiasm.

words.ex: Platonism has influenced many Western philosophers.
words.ex_cn: n. 柏拉图主义影响了许多西方哲学家。
words.en: Platonism is the philosophy of Plato or his followers, especially the theory that abstract forms or ideas are the only true reality.

words.tr: n. 野蛮; 残暴; 暴行; 粗野
words.ex: The barbarity of the war crimes shocked the world.
words.ex_cn: 战争罪行的残暴震惊了世界。
words.en: The quality of being extremely cruel and violent, often associated with uncivilized behavior.

words.tr:
adj. 没有文化的；没有受过教育的；非习得的
v. 忘却；“unlearn”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is unlearned in modern science.
words.ex_cn: 他对现代科学一无所知。
words.en: If you describe someone as unlearned, you mean that they have not received much formal education or that they lack knowledge in a particular subject.

words.ex: We went on an excursion to the mountains last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 上周末我们去山区进行了短途旅行。
words.en: An excursion is a short journey or trip, especially one taken as a leisure activity.

words.ex: The clothiers in the mall offer a wide range of fashionable clothing.
words.ex_cn: 商场里的服装店提供各种时尚服装。
words.en: Clothiers are businesses or individuals who sell clothing and related items.

words.ex: The kitchen has a new washing appliance.
words.ex_cn: 厨房里有一台新的洗衣机。
words.en: An appliance is a device or machine that is used to perform a particular task, especially in the home.

words.ex: The horseshoe is nailed to a horse's hoof.
words.ex_cn: 马蹄形铁掌被钉在马的蹄子上。
words.en: A horseshoe is a piece of metal shaped like a U, which is fixed with nails to the bottom of a horse's foot in order to protect it.

words.ex: He read a biography of Nelson Mandela.
words.ex_cn: 他读了一本关于纳尔逊·曼德拉的传记。
words.en: A biography is a detailed description of a person's life. It involves more than just the basic facts like education, work, relationships, and death; it portrays a person's experience of these life events.

words.ex: The sun moves westwards in the evening.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在傍晚时向西移动。
words.en: towards the west

words.ex: Catherine walks to school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 凯瑟琳每天早上步行去学校。
words.en: A female given name, derived from the Greek name Αικατερινη (Aikaterine).

words.ex: She was indulging in her favorite hobby, painting.
words.ex_cn: 她正沉溺于她最喜欢的爱好——绘画。
words.en: To allow oneself to enjoy the pleasure of something, often excessively.

words.ex: He wore a white waistcoat with his suit.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着一件白色背心搭配西装。
words.en: A waistcoat is a sleeveless garment that buttons down the front, typically worn over a shirt and under a jacket as part of a man's formal or business attire.

words.tr: adj. 精美的；细腻的；强烈的
words.ex: She wore an exquisite dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精美的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is exquisite is extremely beautiful or pleasant, especially in a delicate or refined way.

words.ex: The freshness of the fruit made it delicious.
words.ex_cn: 水果的新鲜让它很好吃。
words.en: The quality of being fresh; newness or recentness; the state of being free from staleness, mustiness, or decay.

words.ex: He showed cowardice when he ran away from the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他在打架时逃跑，表现出了懦弱。
words.en: Cowardice is the lack of courage to face danger, difficulty, opposition, or pain.

words.ex: He expatiated on the importance of education.
words.ex_cn: 他详细阐述了教育的重要性。
words.en: To expatiate means to speak or write about something in great detail or at considerable length.

words.ex: The store specializes in high-quality shirtings for custom tailoring.
words.ex_cn: 这家店专门提供高质量的衬衫布料用于定制裁剪。
words.en: Shirtings refer to fabrics specifically designed for making shirts, often characterized by their texture and durability.

words.ex: He is an innovator who created a new app.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位创造了新应用程序的创新者。
words.en: An innovator is someone who introduces changes and new ideas in the way something is done or made.

words.tr:
n. 野心家
adj. 野心勃勃的
words.ex: He is often criticized as a careerist who will do anything to advance his position.
words.ex_cn: 他经常被批评为一个为了晋升职位而不择手段的野心家。
words.en: A careerist is someone who is very ambitious and is determined to be successful in their career, often to the exclusion of other interests.

words.ex: The falsifier was caught altering the documents.
words.ex_cn: 伪造者被抓到篡改文件。
words.en: A falsifier is someone who alters or forges documents or information with the intent to deceive.

words.ex: The voters are polarised on the new tax law.
words.ex_cn: 选民们对这项新税法意见分裂。
words.en: Divided into two sharply contrasting groups or opinions.

words.ex: He succumbed to pressure and quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他屈服于压力，辞去了工作。
words.en: If you succumb to something, you are unable to resist it and eventually give in to it, often resulting in a negative outcome.

words.tr: n. 华丽；壮丽；光辉；显赫
words.ex: The sunset filled the sky with splendour.
words.ex_cn: 日落让天空充满了壮丽。
words.en: the quality of being magnificent or splendid or grand

words.tr: n. 先生们（法语中对多位男士的尊称）
words.ex: Messieurs, please take your seats.
words.ex_cn: 先生们，请就座。
words.en: A French term used as a title or form of address for a man, equivalent to 'Mr.' in English, and its plural form 'messieurs' is used to address multiple men.

words.ex: She enjoyed the solitudes of the countryside.
words.ex_cn: 她享受乡村的孤独。
words.en: The state of being alone, especially when this is peaceful and pleasant.

words.tr: n. 不喜欢；不赞成；失宠
words.ex: He fell into disfavour with his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他失去了老板的青睐。
words.en: If someone or something is in disfavour, people dislike or disapprove of them.

words.ex: He oversteps his authority by making decisions without consulting the board.
words.ex_cn: 他未经董事会同意就做出决定，超越了他的权限。
words.en: To go beyond what is considered acceptable or allowed.

words.ex: The river overflows its banks every spring.
words.ex_cn: v. 每年春天，河水都会溢出河岸。
words.en: If a liquid or a river overflows, it flows over the edges of the container or place it is in.

words.ex: The throwster carefully twisted the silk threads.
words.ex_cn: 捻丝工小心地捻着丝线。
words.en: A throwster is a person who twists silk or other fibers into thread or yarn.

words.ex: He drew a geometric shape on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上画了一个几何图形。
words.en: Relating to geometry, or according to its methods and principles.

words.ex: He is a candidate for the mayor position.
words.ex_cn: 他是市长职位的候选人。
words.en: A candidate is someone who is being considered for a position, for example someone who is running in an election or applying for a job.

words.tr: v. 题写；铭刻；题名；“inscribe”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He inscribed his name on the stone.
words.ex_cn: 他在石头上题写了名字。
words.en: If something is inscribed on or in something else, it is written or carved there.

words.ex: He was inverting the bottle to pour out the last drops.
words.ex_cn: 他正在倒置瓶子以倒出最后几滴。
words.en: To turn something upside down or inside out, or to reverse the position, order, or relationship of things.

words.ex: The town is known for its historic tanneries.
words.ex_cn: 这个城镇以其历史悠久的制革厂而闻名。
words.en: Tanneries are places where animal hides are processed into leather.

words.tr: n. <正>努力，尽力( endeavor的名词复数 ) v. 尝试，试图( endeavor的第三
words.ex: His endeavors help him succeed.
words.ex_cn: 他的努力帮助他取得成功。
words.en: An endeavor is an attempt to do something, especially something new or original.

words.ex: He arranged the books in a haphazard way.
words.ex_cn: 他随意地摆放了书。
words.en: If you describe something as haphazard, you are critical of it because it is not at all organized or is not arranged according to a plan.

words.ex: The city showed signs of decadence after the war.
words.ex_cn: 战争之后，这座城市显示出衰败的迹象。
words.en: Decadence is a situation in which a society or institution is becoming less moral and less satisfactory.

words.tr: v. （下级对上级的）请求；请求得到；索取；邀请；（下级对上级的）请求( request的过去式和过去分词 )；
words.ex: The student requested permission to leave early.
words.ex_cn: 学生请求提前离开。
words.en: Formally asked for by someone.

words.ex: They are divorcing after ten years of marriage.
words.ex_cn: 他们在结婚十年后正在离婚。
words.en: The act of legally ending a marriage.

words.tr: adj.& adv. 北的，向北的; （指风向）从北面来的
words.ex: The wind is blowing northerly.
words.ex_cn: 风从北方吹来。
words.en: A northerly point, area, or direction is to the north or towards the north. If you move northerly, you move towards the north.

words.tr: v. 预示；宣布；为…的先驱
words.ex: The dark clouds were heralding a storm.
words.ex_cn: v. 乌云预示着暴风雨的来临。
words.en: To be a sign that something is going to happen, especially something important or good.

words.ex: She exclaimed in delight when she saw the surprise.
words.ex_cn: v. 她看到惊喜时高兴地叫了起来。
words.en: If you exclaim, you say something suddenly and loudly, often because you are surprised, excited, or angry.

words.ex: The quilt is a patchwork of old clothes.
words.ex_cn: 这条被子是用旧衣服拼凑而成的。
words.en: Patchwork is a form of needlework that involves sewing together pieces of fabric into a larger design. The larger design is usually based on repeating patterns built up with different fabric shapes (which can be different colors).

words.ex: The company paid indemnity for the damaged car.
words.ex_cn: 公司为损坏的汽车支付了保险赔偿。
words.en: If something provides indemnity, it provides insurance or protection against damage or loss, especially in the form of a legal agreement.

words.ex: Fruits and vegetables provide important nutrients.
words.ex_cn: 水果和蔬菜提供重要的营养素。
words.en: Nutrients are substances that provide nourishment essential for the maintenance of life and for growth.

words.ex: He basically just wants to be left alone.
words.ex_cn: 他基本上只是想一个人待着。
words.en: You use basically to indicate that you are stating a fact or opinion in a simple, clear, or definite way.

words.tr: n. 园艺（学）； v. 从事园艺；“garden”的现在分词；
words.ex: He enjoys gardening in his backyard.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在后院做园艺。
words.en: The activity of tending and cultivating a garden, especially as a pastime.

words.tr: v. 回答；回应；“answer”的现在分词；
words.ex: He is answering the teacher's question.
words.ex_cn: 他正在回答老师的问题。
words.en: If you answer someone, you say something to them in response to something they have said or done.

words.ex: He felt animosity toward his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对邻居感到敌意。
words.en: Animosity is a strong feeling of dislike and anger towards someone.

words.ex: The student went to the infirmary after falling off the bike.
words.ex_cn: 学生骑自行车摔了之后去了医院。
words.en: A place where sick or injured people receive care and treatment, especially in a school, college, or other institution.

words.tr: v. 使沮丧；使萧条；压下
words.ex: The bad news depresses everyone in the office.
words.ex_cn: v. 这个坏消息让办公室里的每个人都感到沮丧。
words.en: To make someone feel very unhappy and without hope; to reduce the level or strength of activity in an economy or market.

words.ex: The pace of the game quickened in the second half.
words.ex_cn: v. 比赛的速度在下半场加快了。
words.en: To make or become faster or more active.

words.ex: He spent ruinously on luxury cars.
words.ex_cn: 他花钱如流水，买豪华汽车。
words.en: In a way that causes great and usually irreparable damage or harm.

words.ex: The student was sent to detention for breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这名学生因违反规则被留校滞留。
words.en: Detention is the act of detaining someone or the state of being detained in official custody, especially as a political prisoner.

words.ex: The movie is a melodrama with crying and loud arguments.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是一部充满哭泣和激烈争吵的煽情剧。
words.en: A melodrama is a dramatic work in which the plot, typically sensational and designed to appeal strongly to the emotions, takes precedence over detailed characterization.

words.tr: adj. 无辔头的；不受控制的；放纵的
words.ex: The unbridled horse ran across the field.
words.ex_cn: 那匹无辔头的马在田野上奔跑。
words.en: If you describe behaviour or feelings as unbridled, you mean that they are not controlled or limited in any way.

words.ex: The play shows many tragedies in ancient times.
words.ex_cn: 这部戏剧展现了古代的许多悲剧。
words.en: A tragedy is a very sad event or situation, especially one involving death or suffering.

words.ex: He is domiciled in New York for tax purposes.
words.ex_cn: 他为了税务目的定居在纽约。
words.en: If someone is domiciled in a particular place, they live there and consider it to be their permanent home.

words.ex: He walked home with his companion.
words.ex_cn: 他和同伴一起走回家。
words.en: A companion is someone who you spend time with or who you are travelling with.

words.ex: The lab uses sulphuric acid for cleaning.
words.ex_cn: 实验室用硫酸进行清洁。
words.en: Sulphuric is an adjective used to describe something that contains or relates to sulphur.

words.ex: The observers watched the game quietly.
words.ex_cn: 观察者们安静地观看了比赛。
words.en: People who watch and pay attention to something, especially in order to learn or understand it.

words.tr:
adj. 惹人喜爱的
v. 使受喜爱；“endear”的现在分词
words.ex: Her smile is endearing.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑很可爱。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as endearing, you mean that it causes you to feel very fond of them.

words.ex: My son loves watching cartoon animation.
words.ex_cn: 我儿子喜欢看卡通动画。
words.en: Animation is the process of making films in which drawings or puppets appear to move.

words.ex: The firefighters cleared the brushwood to stop the fire.
words.ex_cn: 消防员清除了砍下的树枝以阻止火势蔓延。
words.en: Brushwood refers to small branches and twigs broken off from trees or bushes, often used for making fires or as material for building.

words.tr: n. 药剂师；配药师；分配者；自动售货机
words.ex: The dispenser gave me medicine for my cough.
words.ex_cn: 药剂师给了我治疗咳嗽的药。
words.en: A dispenser is a machine or container that automatically provides a specific amount of a product, such as food, drink, or money, when you operate it.

words.ex: He falsifies the documents to avoid taxes.
words.ex_cn: 他伪造文件以逃避税收。
words.en: To falsify means to alter or manipulate something, especially information or a document, in order to deceive people.

words.ex: The desolated village was abandoned after the war.
words.ex_cn: 战争后，这个荒凉的村庄被遗弃了。
words.en: If a place is desolated, it is empty of people and lacking in comfort.

words.tr: adj. 声称的；公开承认的；伪称的；自诩的；假充的；（修士）已宣誓入教的; v. 声称；断言；伪称...
words.ex: He is a professed fan of classical music.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名自称的古典音乐爱好者。
words.en: If you profess to do or have something, you claim that you do it or have it, often when you do not.

words.ex: The prentices were eager to learn the craft from the master.
words.ex_cn: 学徒们渴望从师傅那里学习手艺。
words.en: A prentice is a person who is learning a trade or skill from a master or experienced worker.

words.ex: His heterodox ideas shocked the traditional scholars.
words.ex_cn: 他的非正统观点让传统学者感到震惊。
words.en: Heterodox ideas, opinions, or practices are different from the accepted or official ones.

words.tr: v. 安排（arrange 的 ing 形式）
words.ex: He is arranging books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他正在把书摆放在架子上。
words.en: If you arrange an event or meeting, you make plans for it to happen.

words.ex: His utterance made everyone silent.
words.ex_cn: 他的话让所有人都沉默了。
words.en: An utterance is a word, statement, or sound that someone says.

words.tr: v. 重新铸造；彻底改动
words.ex: The director is recasting the play to better suit the modern audience.
words.ex_cn: 导演正在重新选角，以更适合现代观众。
words.en: To cast or fashion anew.

words.tr: v. 预先阻止；抢先一步
words.ex: He forestalls problems by planning ahead.
words.ex_cn: 他通过提前计划来防止问题。
words.en: To forestall something means to prevent it from happening or to act before someone else does in order to prevent them from doing something.

words.tr: adj. 辩论的；引起争论的；争议的
words.ex: His polemical article sparked strong debates.
words.ex_cn: 他那篇有争议的文章引发了激烈争论。
words.en: A polemical piece of writing or speech is one that strongly argues against or in favor of a particular opinion, person, or idea, often in a way that is intended to provoke controversy.

words.tr:
adj. 不愉快的；伤害人感情的
v. 冒犯；得罪；违反；“offend”的现在分词
words.ex: The loud music was offending to the neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的音乐让邻居们感到不愉快。
words.en: If you describe something as offending, you mean that it is unpleasant or not acceptable in some way.

words.ex: The teacher supervises the students during the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 老师在实验期间指导学生。
words.en: If you supervise an activity or a person, you make sure that the activity is done correctly or that the person is doing a task or behaving correctly.

words.tr:
adj. 唯利是图的；雇佣的
n. 雇佣兵；唯利是图者
words.ex: He works as a mercenary for money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了钱当雇佣兵。
words.en: A mercenary is a professional soldier hired to serve in a foreign army.

words.tr: n. 执行者；遗嘱执行人
words.ex: The executors of the will ensured that all assets were distributed according to the deceased's wishes.
words.ex_cn: 遗嘱执行人确保所有资产按照逝者的意愿分配。
words.en: Executors are individuals appointed to carry out the terms of a will or to manage the affairs of a deceased person.

words.tr: adj. 力大无比的；艰巨的
words.ex: The task ahead is herculean, but we are determined to succeed.
words.ex_cn: 前方的任务艰巨无比，但我们决心要成功。
words.en: If you describe a task or job as herculean, you mean that it is extremely difficult and requires a lot of effort.

words.tr: n. 伊斯兰教徒；穆斯林
words.ex: The mahometan prayed five times a day.
words.ex_cn: 伊斯兰教徒每天祈祷五次。
words.en: A Mahometan is a follower of the Islamic religion, also known as a Muslim.

words.ex: He cudgelled the thief to make him confess.
words.ex_cn: 他用短棒打小偷，迫使他招供。
words.en: To beat or strike with a short, thick stick.

words.tr: adj. 无意义的；无目的的
words.ex: His unmeaning smile made her feel uneasy.
words.ex_cn: 他无意义的微笑让她感到不安。
words.en: If you describe something as unmeaning, you mean that it has no purpose or significance.

words.tr: adj. 变荣耀的，美其名的; v. 赞美；美化（glorify 的过去分词）
words.ex: He calls his job a glorified babysitter.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的工作称为一个被夸大的保姆。
words.en: If you describe something as glorified, you mean that it is considered to be more important or special than it really is.

words.ex: The severance of the cable caused the power to go out.
words.ex_cn: 电缆的切断导致了停电。
words.en: The act of ending a connection or relationship; the state of being separated or divided.

words.ex: The wound caused a serious infection.
words.ex_cn: 伤口引起了严重的感染。
words.en: An infection is a disease caused by microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses, or parasites invading the body.

words.ex: The immortals live forever in the myth.
words.ex_cn: 这些永生者在神话中永远活着。
words.en: Immortals are beings who live forever and do not die.

words.ex: He is harassing his classmate every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都在骚扰他的同学。
words.en: If someone harasses you, they trouble or annoy you, for example by attacking you repeatedly or by causing you as many problems as they can.

words.ex: The company made several virements to cover the unexpected expenses.
words.ex_cn: 公司进行了几次转账以支付意外开支。
words.en: The act of transferring funds from one account to another, especially within the same organization.

words.ex: The soil is too infertile to grow crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片土地太贫瘠了，无法种植庄稼。
words.en: Infertile land or soil is not able to produce good crops or plants. An infertile person, animal, or plant cannot have babies, eggs, or seeds.

words.tr:
adj. 挪威（人，语）的；
n. 挪威语；
words.ex: He speaks Norwegian fluently.
words.ex_cn: 他流利地说挪威语。
words.en: Belonging or relating to Norway, its people, or its language.

words.tr: adj. 全神贯注的； v. “engross”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was engrossed in reading a book.
words.ex_cn: 他全神贯注地看书。
words.en: If you are engrossed in something, you are completely absorbed in it and giving it all your attention.

words.ex: She was flaunting her new dress at the party.
words.ex_cn: 她在聚会上炫耀她的新裙子。
words.en: To display (something) ostentatiously, especially in order to provoke envy or admiration or to show defiance.

words.tr: v. 加快进展( expedite的过去式和过去分词 ); 迅速完成
words.ex: The package was expedited to arrive faster.
words.ex_cn: 这个包裹被加急处理以更快送达。
words.en: If you expedite something, you cause it to be done more quickly.

words.ex: The new law is entitling workers to more vacation days.
words.ex_cn: 新法律赋予工人更多的休假天数。
words.en: To give someone the right to do or have something; to give a title to a book, film, etc.

words.ex: She was pondering over the problem all night.
words.ex_cn: 她整晚都在思考这个问题。
words.en: To think about something carefully, especially before making a decision or reaching a conclusion.

words.ex: The project began at its inception.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目从开始时就启动了。
words.en: The inception of something is the start or beginning of it.

words.ex: His calm demeanour surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他冷静的举止让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: Demeanour refers to the way in which a person behaves towards others; their outward behaviour or bearing.

words.tr: n. 教条主义；武断；独断论
words.ex: His dogmatism makes it hard to talk with him.
words.ex_cn: 他的教条主义让他很难交流。
words.en: Dogmatism is the tendency to lay down principles as undeniably true, without consideration of evidence or the opinions of others.

words.ex: The islanders fish every morning.
words.ex_cn: 岛民每天早上捕鱼。
words.en: People who live on an island.

words.ex: The argument is full of fallacies.
words.ex_cn: 这个论点充满了谬误。
words.en: A fallacy is a mistaken belief, especially one based on unsound argument.

words.ex: The cheetah shows swiftness when it runs.
words.ex_cn: 猎豹奔跑时表现出迅速。
words.en: Swiftness is the quality of moving or being able to move quickly.

words.ex: The venerable teacher has taught for over 40 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位值得尊敬的老师已经教书40多年了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as venerable, you mean that they are old and respected.

words.ex: The sun dispelled the morning fog.
words.ex_cn: 太阳驱散了晨雾。
words.en: To dispel means to make something, especially a feeling or belief, go away or disappear.

words.tr: v. 从事；乘船( embark的现在分词 )；
words.ex: He is embarking on a new business.
words.ex_cn: 他正在从事一项新的生意。
words.en: To start a journey, especially on a ship or aircraft; to start doing something new or different.

words.ex: The fog enveloped the whole town.
words.ex_cn: 雾笼罩了整个小镇。
words.en: To wrap up, cover, or surround completely.

words.tr: adj. 不可改变的；永恒不变的
words.ex: The password is immutable and cannot be changed.
words.ex_cn: 密码是不可更改的。
words.en: If you say that something is immutable, you mean that it cannot be changed at all.

words.ex: Her talent in painting is eclipsing that of her peers.
words.ex_cn: 她的绘画才华使她的同龄人黯然失色。
words.en: To obscure or block out (a source of light), especially by interposing something between it and the observer; to surpass or outshine someone or something.

words.tr: n. 一种红色衬衫，以意大利民族英雄朱塞佩·加里波第命名；一种甜饼干，内含果酱
words.ex: She wore a bright garibaldi to the picnic.
words.ex_cn: 她在野餐时穿了一件鲜艳的加里波第衬衫。
words.en: A garibaldi is a type of red shirt named after the Italian national hero Giuseppe Garibaldi, or a type of sweet biscuit containing jam.

words.ex: She felt revulsion when she saw the dirty food.
words.ex_cn: 当她看到那脏兮兮的食物时，感到非常厌恶。
words.en: A sudden and intense feeling of disgust or loathing.

words.tr: n. 三角形( triangle的名词复数 ); 三人一组; 三角铁（打击乐器）; 三角板
words.ex: He drew three triangles on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上画了三个三角形。
words.en: Plural of triangle: a plane figure with three straight sides and three angles.

words.tr: adj. 一文不名的；穷困的；
words.ex: He was penniless after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后一文不名。
